maya: FYI — AcmeProd (customer) just opened a sev2: huge increase in client-side JSON parse errors after flipping on JSON-mode for our chat endpoint. Getting ~3% downstream failures and a couple 5xx spikes. Ticket #3245 :eyes:

maya: Repro window looks like 2026-03-16 09:12–09:25 UTC. They attached a sample response that caused their client to blow up. Pasting the model output we logged (sanitized):

maya: ```
{"items": [{"id": "123", "name": "Widget"}, {"id": "124", "name": "Gizmo",}]  // trailing comma -> invalid JSON
```

sanjay: thanks — that trailing comma is a classic. Do we know whether this is the model generating the comma or something in the post-processing layer?

alex: likely model. We see cases where it emits a literal trailing comma or a short comment text after the JSON. Our current JSON-mode postproc tries to extract the first JSON block but not robust to trailing commas.

alex: quick diagnostics: what do logs show for raw_model_output vs parsed_output? can we capture the raw output + request_id?

maya: we currently log a redacted raw_output for 1% of requests. For this customer we captured a couple samples (redacted). I've pasted one above.

elena: Product question — is this an isolated AcmeCorp issue or surfacing across customers? dashboards?

ops-bot: ALERT: structured_output_parse_rate for /v1/chat/generate > 0.8% (5m) — flagged for review.

sanjay: we should instrument a dedicated metric: structured_output.parse_failures{route,model,customer}. Right now we only have a generic "generation_errors" metric which mixes model + infra. Add a tag for parse_failure and a reason enum (invalid_json, schema_mismatch, truncated).

alex: agree. Also add a span in traces for "json_parse" after model output so we can attach the raw output sample (or a hash pointer) to the trace. That will let SRE correlate latency/parse failures with model versions.

elena: dashboard item: show parse_failure_rate by customer and model, plus a table of recent sample hashes. Alert when rate > 0.5% for 10m for any paid customer. Add a runbook link for support -> eng oncall.

maya: customer asks for workaround ASAP. Suggested temporary options to them: 1) disable JSON-mode, 2) use stricter schema and server-side validation with sanitization fallback, or 3) add a client-side tolerant JSON parser (robust to trailing commas) while we investigate. They prefer to keep JSON-mode on.

alex: short-term engineering mitigations: 1) tighten post-process: run a JSON sanitizer that removes trailing commas + comments before final parse (low-risk), 2) if sanitize fails, return the raw output with an explicit parse_failure code so we don't return 5xx to customers, 3) increment parse_failures metric with reason.

sanjay: long-term: try RL/LLM prompt tuning to enforce stricter JSON output + add an internal validation loop that retries generation with a repair prompt if parse fails. But that is a follow-up.

maya: security note: when we increase raw output logging for troubleshooting, we must not store PII. Proposal: store a SHA256 hash of the full raw_output and keep full plaintext only in a short-lived secure bucket (kms-protected) accessible to eng oncall. Redacted logs keep placeholders for email/SSN.

elena: agree. Add a policy in the runbook: "for parse-failure escalations, capture up to 5 full samples to secure bucket; all other samples store only hash+redacted_text."

alex: I've got a small PR ready for the sanitizer + metric tagging. Will open PR and request review.

sanjay: I'll add the metric + alert and the trace span today.

maya: Action items:
- maya: send AcmeCorp repro steps + advise client workaround (disable or tolerant parse) — ASAP
- alex: PR for sanitizer + parse_failure tagging (ETA 4h)
- sanjay: add metric, tracing span, and alert (ETA 3h)
- elena: update dashboard + runbook text (ETA EOD)

elena: once changes land, we'll notify customer and offer to replay their failing requests under the secure debug mode.

maya: thanks team. tagging @alex @sanjay for oncall. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-link: https://internal.incidents/3245 — created 2026-03-16T09:21:05Z

sanjay: I'll post status updates in this thread as I make progress.

maya: heard — keeping customer posted now.
